A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Stein Diffusion Guidance work. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original SDG image-guidance and molecular-generation results, including ablations, sampling-dynamics analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds text-to-image style-transfer results and Parp1 molecular-generation results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the Stein correction, and the molecular procedure remain unchanged. Appendix D adds a task-specific inference adaptation for style transfer: Stein correction is inserted into full TFG before its guidance stages, retaining components removed from the earlier image-task implementation.

E1.justification: v3 adds text-to-image style transfer using WikiArt reference styles and Partiprompts text prompts, introducing joint style and text conditioning. It also adds Parp1 to the three existing docking targets. The newly cited image-data sources for retained reconstruction tasks do not establish additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the retained image-task comparisons from DPS and LGD to include MPGD and UGD, materially broadening comparison with more elaborate guidance methods. For the new style-transfer experiment, SDG without correction represents full TFG. The molecular comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new style-transfer protocol uses four style exemplars, 64 prompts, 14-particle update batches, and Style Score and CLIP Score metrics. Parp1 receives target-specific settings in v3 Table 5. Existing molecular evaluation criteria and the documented image-label timing protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 extends the correction, low-density, and Langevin variant comparisons to Parp1 and adds qualitative airplane-generation comparisons with and without correction in Figures 8–9. Existing particle-count ablations, low-density robustness tests, and reward/score dynamics are retained; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report molecular hit ratios and top-5% docking scores as means and standard deviations over three runs. Parp1 follows the same practice. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed repeated-run counts are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds MPGD/UGD image scores, style-transfer results, and Parp1 results while retaining the original benchmark values. Parp1 SDG achieves 8.780±1.033% novel hits versus MOOD's 7.017±0.428%. Within the new style-transfer experiment, correction improves Style Score from 3.16 to 3.05 but reduces CLIP Score from 29.0 to 28.8. The new MPGD comparison also shows better deblurring LPIPS than SDG, 0.177 versus 0.246.

T1.justification: v3 formalizes the transport perturbation in Lemma 2.1, adds regularity assumptions and real-valued costs in Section 2.3, and adds a bounded-test-function particle convergence statement. Proposition 3.1 and Appendix B redefine the guided density through a conditional expectation and revise the associated derivation. The central surrogate objective and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the low-density SOC cost, the variational bound motivating posterior correction, and the Stein correction framework. v3 foregrounds image evidence in its abstract and introduction, but image applicability was already claimed in v2 Section 4.1 and its conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 changes the claimed robustness relative to Langevin correction from 'provably' to 'empirically' and explicitly discusses the RKHS restriction and its high-dimensional limitations. Section 4.3 adds an explanation of practical memory scaling. Conversely, v2's discussion of the image-label accuracy/FID tradeoff is omitted.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the median-distance kernel-bandwidth heuristic, Parp1 hyperparameters, and the precise TFG integration point and particle limit for style transfer. Appendix D also identifies data sources for retained image tasks. Most existing implementation details remain unchanged, and no new code-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section adds context on classifier-free guidance, Feynman–Kac correctors, and geometry-informed SVGD. References also expand for MPGD, UGD, particle convergence, and image datasets. The central positioning as an efficient SOC-motivated alternative to uncorrected Tweedie guidance remains intact.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: qualitative results move from the final appendix to Appendix A, the impact statement moves into the main text, computational analysis gains Section 4.3, and a Related Work section is added. Molecular experiment subsections are consolidated, limitations are expanded, and symbolic names replace lengthy SDG variant descriptions.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text and references, extensively relocating and resizing displays. Tables gain comparator rows, task/target columns, and colored highlights; existing runtime results are also consolidated into a main-text table. New airplane and style-transfer figures are added, while existing docking and robustness figures are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added MPGD/UGD comparisons and style-transfer and Parp1 evaluations strengthen assessment of generality, while clearer assumptions, implementation details, and limitations improve precision. These are incremental gains over an already substantial experimental paper. v3 incompletely discusses metric tradeoffs, including the lower CLIP Score accompanying improved style matching in Table 1, which limits the overall improvement.
